prompt: Arlo counted his coins in three steps. Step one: he made piles of ten and got 2 full piles. Step two: he said 2 piles of ten make 20. Step three: he added the 5 loose coins and said 20 plus 5 is 30. The wrong step is
options: step one, because the piles were made wrong.
step two, because 2 tens do not make 20.
step three, because 20 plus 5 is 25.

prompt: Nell watered one plant in three steps. Step one: she filled the watering can. Step two: she poured the water on the leaves only, not on the soil. Step three: she put the can away. Later the soil was still dry. The step that went wrong is
options: step two, because the water never reached the soil.
step one, because the can was filled too full.
step three, because the can was put away too soon.

prompt: Dev drew a square in steps. First he drew the top side. Next he drew the left side. Then he drew the bottom side and stopped. His shape has a gap where a side should be. The problem comes from
options: the first part, because the top side was too long.
the last part, because he stopped before the right side.
the middle part, because the left side was crooked.

prompt: Cora shared 12 stickers in steps. Step one: she counted 12 stickers. Step two: she said that she and her two friends make three people, so each person gets 12 split three ways, which is 4. Step three: she gave each friend 4 stickers and kept 5 for herself. The wrong step is
options: step one, because the sticker count was off.
step two, because only two people were sharing.
step three, because 4 plus 4 plus 5 is 13, not 12.

prompt: Otis followed a recipe card that said: mix, then bake, then cool. Step one: he mixed the batter. Step two: he set the pan in the cold room for an hour to cool. Step three: he baked it. The cake came out flat. The step in the wrong place is
options: step two, because cooling belongs after baking.
step three, because baking was not on the card.
step one, because mixing belongs at the end.

prompt: Ravi measured a rug with his feet. Step one: he walked heel to toe along the rug and counted 8 foot lengths. Step two: he walked back the same way and counted 10. Step three: he wrote down 8 and moved on. The careless step is
options: step one, because heel to toe walking cannot measure a rug.
step three, because the two counts did not agree and he ignored that.
step two, because walking back along the rug spoiled the count.

prompt: Bea planned a snack for 4 children, 2 crackers each. Step one: she said 4 times 2 is 8 crackers. Step two: she took 8 crackers from a full pack of 10. Step three: when one more child arrived, she kept the same 8 crackers and still planned 2 for each of the 5 children. Step four: she ran short and was surprised. The first wrong step is
options: step one, because 4 times 2 is not 8.
step two, because the pack was too small to give 8.
step three, because 5 children at 2 each need 10 crackers.

prompt: Zane kept score for a game in steps. Step one: red scored 3, so he wrote red 3, blue 0. Step two: blue scored 2, so he wrote red 3, blue 2. Step three: red scored 1 more, so he wrote red 5, blue 2. Step four: he announced that red led by 3. The first wrong step is
options: step three, because 3 plus 1 is 4, not 5.
step four, because the lead was not 3.
step two, because blue's number was wrong.

prompt: Wren's paper boat sank because the paper soaked up water. Next time, to keep her boat afloat, she should
options: fold the boat from a bigger sheet of the same paper.
fold the boat from wax paper, which does not soak.
sail the boat in deeper, calmer water.

prompt: The tower of blocks fell because the biggest block sat on top. To make it stand, the fix is to
options: put the biggest block at the bottom.
add one more big block to the top.
stack the same order again with steadier hands.

prompt: Iris's kite would not climb because the string was too short. The fix that matches the problem is to
options: add a heavier tail to the kite.
wait for a day with less wind.
tie on a longer string.

prompt: Suki's plant drooped, and she found the soil dry as dust. She had been misting only the leaves. The fix that fits what she found is to
options: pour water on the soil so the roots can drink.
mist the leaves more times each day.
move the plant to a sunnier spot.

prompt: The door of the toy house swung open because its latch was bent. Arlo glued the door shut, and then no one could open it to play. A better fix would be to
options: use a stronger glue so the door stays shut.
straighten the bent latch so the door still opens.
paint the door so the bend does not show.

prompt: Dev baked rolls that came out hard. He checked his notes: the oven heat matched the recipe, the baking time matched too, but he had used only half the butter because the tub ran low. For the next batch the fix is to
options: turn the oven heat down so the rolls stay soft.
take the rolls out earlier than the recipe says.
get enough butter and use the full amount.

prompt: The class robot drifted to the left on every run. Juno watched the wheels and saw the left wheel turning slower than the right, and she knew a robot curves toward its slower side. The fix that follows from this is to
options: speed up the left wheel to match the right.
slow down the left wheel a little more.
point the robot to the right before each run.

prompt: Otis's paper airplane dove to the floor after every short flight. A friend said the nose was too heavy, so Otis tore off the whole nose, and then the plane just fluttered and went nowhere. Thinking about both tries, the best fix is to
options: put back even more weight than the nose first had.
take a little weight off the nose, not all of it.
throw the fluttering plane much harder.

prompt: When Bea studied her spelling words out loud, she got them all right. When she read them silently, she missed many. For next week's list she should
options: study the words out loud.
read the words silently.
study only the words she got right.

prompt: Carrying one plate at a time, Ravi broke nothing. Carrying four plates at once, he dropped two. For the rest of the dishes he should
options: carry four plates but walk more slowly.
carry all the plates in one tall stack.
carry one plate at a time.

prompt: Wren tried two ways to find her lost sock. Poking around in random spots turned up nothing all morning. Searching one room at a time, corner to corner, found it in ten minutes. When she loses her hat, she should
options: poke around in random spots first.
search one room at a time, corner to corner.
wait for the hat to turn up on its own.

prompt: On Monday's quiz, Zane guessed fast and got 4 out of 10. On Tuesday's quiz, he checked each answer before moving on and got 9 out of 10, finishing just in time. On the next quiz he should
options: check each answer before moving on.
guess fast to leave time to spare.
check only the hardest answer and guess the rest.

prompt: Arlo's team scored when he kicked the ball as hard as he could, but that goal came from a lucky bounce. Across the whole season, his soft aimed kicks scored far more often than hard ones. In the next game he should
options: kick as hard as he can every time.
stop shooting and only pass the ball.
keep using soft aimed kicks.

prompt: Nell tried three ways to remember her library day. A note on her door worked every single week. Asking her brother worked only on the rare days he remembered. Trusting her own memory failed almost every time. Her brother now says he will do better, but the note has never failed. The most dependable plan is to
options: count on her brother, since he says he will do better.
keep putting the note on her door.
trust her own memory, since she knows the day well now.

prompt: Juno practiced her song two ways over two weeks. Playing it from the start every time made the easy parts smooth, but the hard middle stayed rough. Drilling only the hard middle made the middle smooth. Her show is in one week, and only the middle still trips her up. This week she should
options: spend most days drilling the hard middle.
play the song from the start every time.
learn a new song while this one rests.

prompt: A sign says the pool is closed on Mondays. Today is Monday, and Cora tells her friends the pool is open. Her claim should be
options: accepted, because the sign is about other pools.
rejected, because the sign says Mondays are closed.
accepted, because pool signs are often old.

prompt: Dev says 6 plus 7 makes 12. Counting up seven from 6 lands on 13. His answer should be
options: accepted, because 12 is close enough to 13.
accepted, because counting up can slip by one.
rejected, because the careful count lands on 13.

prompt: Iris claims she read 40 pages this week because she read 5 pages every day. A week has 7 days. Her claim should be
options: doubted, because 5 a day for 7 days makes 35.
believed, because 5 times 7 is 40.
believed, because 40 pages in a week is easy.

prompt: Zane measured the same string twice and got 30 and then 32. He wrote in his report that the string is exactly 30. His report should be
options: accepted, because the first measure is the true one.
questioned, because his own two measures disagreed.
accepted, because 32 was clearly the bad read.

prompt: Bea claims her snail is the fastest in class because it crossed the finish line first on race day. But her snail started at the middle line, while every other snail started twice as far back. Before agreeing, a careful judge would call the win
options: strong proof, because it did cross the line first.
strong proof, because all the snails raced at the same time.
weak proof, because her snail had a shorter track.

prompt: A cook claims his pot of soup fills 10 bowls, because a bigger pot once filled 10. Each bowl takes 2 scoops, and today's pot holds 16 scoops. Checking today's pot, his claim should be
options: accepted, because the bigger pot managed 10 before.
rejected, because 16 scoops makes 12 bowls, not 10.
rejected, because 16 scoops makes only 8 bowls.

prompt: Otis claims heavier things always fall faster, because his rock beat a falling leaf to the ground. Suki then dropped a heavy rock and a light coin together, and they landed at the same time. Taking both tests into account, the claim is
options: supported, because the rock did beat the leaf.
not supported, because the coin test disagrees with it.
supported, because rocks are heavier than coins.
